{"id":"mimid-1wgh.106","title":"Decide when follower catch-up is implemented, relative to the January 2027 Haven interop day","description":"docs/design/mimi-catchup.md §12.3.

The note's own framing of this question was WRONG and was corrected
before Mark decided. It said catch-up was "new protocol surface six
weeks out" and that "the interop-day scope has to shrink to pay for
it". Reading mimid-1wgh.46.20:

- that bead says "mimid needs no new features for them": the interop
  day runs cross-hub delivery, committer authority, the room-policy
  cross-check and refusal codes, all of which already exist. Catch-up
  was never competing with interop-day features.
- the date is NOT set, and the day is gated on Haven first delivering
  messages and Commits from rooms on other hubs and keeping the ratchet
  tree (Jason Bolduc's list, #mimi 238476). "Six weeks out" was an
  assumption, not a fact.

So the real trade was narrower: regression risk in the hub's fanout
write path, which mimid-1wgh.46.20.2 (cross-hub delivery both ways, no
422) exercises.

Options offered: implement now but inert (template unpublished);
implement after the interop day; implement now fully live; or land only
.1 and .2 now.

DECIDED by Mark, 2026-11-22: implement now, FULLY LIVE. The catchUp
directory template is published and the endpoint is reachable by peers.

Why: it gives Haven something concrete to react to in January and makes
the protocol-08 proposal (decision mimid-1wgh.105) evidence-backed
rather than theoretical.

CONSEQUENCES, which the implementation beads must honour:

- §8's participation-window MUST is a live authorization boundary from
  the first deploy, not a design aspiration. mimid-1wgh.37.104.3 MUST
  NOT be deployed before .2 exists; the dependency is wired so bd will
  not offer it first.
- The endpoint is peer-reachable, so it is untrusted input: it gets the
  same provider authentication as the rest of the peer surface (epic
  mimid-75nk) and the same strict decoding and named limits as any
  other wire surface.
- The fanout write path changes before mimid-1wgh.46.20.2 runs. A new
  outbound header is additive and Haven ignores unknown headers, so the
  wire change itself costs interop nothing; the exposure is our own
  regression risk, covered by mimid-1wgh.37.104.5's two-provider test.","status":"closed","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-11-23T01:26:39.020041681Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-11-23T01:26:46.327399756Z","closed_at":"2026-11-23T01:26:46.327399756Z","close_reason":"Closed","labels":["human"],"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"mimid-1wgh.106","depends_on_id":"mimid-1wgh","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-11-23T01:26:39.06133642Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","metadata":"{}"}]}
new_value: {"notes":"Superseded in part by decision mimid-1wgh.107 (same day): this bead's consequence list said §8's participation-window MUST becomes a live authorization boundary on the first deploy. It is now a SHOULD, and an efficiency and metadata-hygiene bound rather than an authorization boundary, because a provider holds no MLS group keys. The rest of this bead stands: the endpoint is peer-reachable untrusted input from the first deploy and gets provider authentication, strict decoding and named limits, and .2 still precedes .3."}
